Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Story: FDA/HHS Peptide Compounding Interim Policy: HIMS Winners/Losers and OMB Review Timeline. Related tickers: HIMS.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

Why this needs follow-up: HHS and FDA submitted a peptide compounding interim access policy to OMB on October 15 but terms were not disclosed — Hims & Hers and specialty pharmacy stocks are directly affected and the policy timeline and specific peptide list are missing numbers a sophisticated investor needs.

ANSWER EACH QUESTION (run a separate search for each):
- What specific peptides does the HHS/FDA interim access policy submitted to OMB on October 15 2026 cover beyond BPC-157, and what are the proposed conditions for specialty pharmacy compounding authorization?
- What is the OMB review timeline for the HHS/FDA peptide compounding interim policy, and when would any final rule or interim final rule take effect?
- Which publicly traded specialty pharmacy or telehealth companies beyond Hims & Hers did analysts name as beneficiaries or losers from the October 15 2026 FDA peptide compounding policy filing?

Name every stock affected by this story with its move, analyst notes that name winners and losers
(firm, rating, PT), exact figures (deal values, estimates, dates), and the latest status as of the
cutoff. Prefer Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, WSJ, Barron's, MarketWatch, company releases, filings.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or sub-topic:

## TICKER or Sub-topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.

content:
## HIMS [Telehealth]

- Hims & Hers Health (HIMS) closed up **6%** on Thursday, October 15, after reports that HHS had submitted an interim peptide-access policy to OMB; the latest cited close was not accompanied by an intraday or pre-market price in the available reporting. (Seeking Alpha, Oct. 15 17:38 ET)[1]
- Hims & Hers had previously said it planned to offer peptides if regulations permitted; the company had not publicly confirmed the policy’s terms by the cutoff. (Reuters, Oct. 15; CNBC, Oct. 15 15:36 ET)[1][5]

## NOOM [Telehealth]

- Noom was identified as another telehealth company that had announced plans to offer peptides if federal restrictions were eased; no publicly traded ticker, stock move, analyst rating, or price target was reported in the available coverage. (CNBC, Oct. 15 15:36 ET)[5]

## Policy scope [HHS/FDA]

- HHS and FDA submitted **“Interim Access Policy for Compounding Using Certain Peptides”** to OMB for review; the OMB entry lists **RIN 0910-ZD94**, a **received date of October 14, 2026**, and a **posting/update date of October 15, 2026**. (OMB, Oct. 15)[10]
- The OMB filing disclosed **no peptide list, operating conditions, implementation date, or duration**. (Reuters, Oct. 15; CNBC, Oct. 15 15:36 ET)[1][5]
- Two people familiar with the plan told the Associated Press that the policy would temporarily allow specialty pharmacies to compound selected peptides, including **BPC-157**; this reporting is **[report]** and the proposal remained unconfirmed by HHS and FDA. (Reuters, Oct. 15; CNBC, Oct. 15 15:36 ET)[1][5]
- The reported mechanism is **FDA enforcement discretion**, under which the agency would temporarily refrain from pursuing qualifying pharmacies for producing designated peptides; this would not constitute FDA approval or formal addition to the permitted compounding list. (CNBC, Oct. 15 15:36 ET; Becker’s Hospital Review, Oct. 15)[5][2]
- The FDA’s July 2026 advisory panel recommended easing restrictions on **six of seven** peptides reviewed: **BPC-157, KPV, TB-500, MOTS-c, Semax, and Epitalon**; it did not recommend easing restrictions on **emideltide, also called DSIP**. (Frier Levitt, Oct. 14, updated Oct. 15; YourNews, Oct. 15)[7][8]
- The six peptides named in the July advisory recommendations are the reported candidates beyond BPC-157, but the October 15 OMB filing did not confirm that all six were covered by the interim policy. (Frier Levitt, Oct. 14, updated Oct. 15; Reuters, Oct. 15)[7][1]
- The proposed authorization conditions for specialty pharmacies were not disclosed; available reporting described only temporary enforcement discretion for “qualifying” compounding pharmacies. (CNBC, Oct. 15 15:36 ET; Compound Brief, Oct. 15)[5][9]

## OMB review timeline [Regulatory]

- The OMB entry classifies the matter as **Pending EO 12866 Regulatory Review**, with agency/subagency **HHS/FDA**, stage **Notice**, and **no legal deadline**. (OMB, Oct. 15)[10]
- The filing is marked **not economically significant** and lists no statutory review deadline. (OMB, Oct. 15)[10]
- No OMB completion date, publication date, implementation date, or effective date had been announced by **02:03 ET on October 16, 2026**. (OMB, Oct. 15; Reuters, Oct. 15)[10][1]
- A formal rule adding peptides to the FDA’s compounding list would require federal rulemaking and public comment; reporting characterized that process as potentially taking **years**, while a legal analysis estimated **12 to 18 months or longer**. (CNBC, Oct. 15 15:36 ET; Frier Levitt, Oct. 14, updated Oct. 15)[5][7]
- The interim policy could theoretically operate before completion of permanent rulemaking through enforcement discretion, but no final-rule or interim-final-rule effective date had been disclosed. (CNBC, Oct. 15 15:36 ET; Becker’s Hospital Review, Oct. 15)[5][2]

## Specialty pharmacy and telehealth stocks [Market impact]

- The available October 15–16 coverage named **HIMS** as the only publicly traded company with a reported stock move: **+6% at Thursday’s close**. (Seeking Alpha, Oct. 15 17:38 ET)[4]
- The available coverage did not identify any additional publicly traded specialty-pharmacy company as an analyst-designated beneficiary or loser, and it reported no analyst firm, rating change, or price-target change for HIMS or another ticker during the specified window. (Reuters, Oct. 15; CNBC, Oct. 15 15:36 ET)[1][5]
- The peptide market was estimated at **$2 billion to $3 billion** in reporting citing the Associated Press; the estimate was not attributed to a named equity analyst. (Becker’s Hospital Review, Oct. 15)[2]
